title: Zanzibar and the Swahili Coast: A Short History
excerpt: From trade with Arabia and India to the Omani sultanate and colonial rule: a short history of Zanzibar and the Swahili coast.
body:
Zanzibar's history is the history of the Indian Ocean. For centuries, monsoon winds carried traders between East Africa, Arabia, Persia and India.

## Swahili culture

Along the coast, a Swahili culture developed from African, Arab and Persian influences, with trading towns and a shared language, Swahili. See [the history of Swahili](/blog/swahili-language-history/).

## Portuguese and Omani rule

The Portuguese controlled parts of the coast in the 16th and 17th centuries. Later, the Sultanate of Oman took over, and in the 19th century the sultan moved his capital to Zanzibar.

## Cloves and slavery

Zanzibar became a centre for cloves and also for the East African slave trade. The slave market closed in 1873 under British pressure. Visiting the memorial in Stone Town is an important part of understanding the island.

## British protectorate

From 1890, Zanzibar was a British protectorate, while the sultan remained.

## Independence and union

Zanzibar became independent in 1963, followed by a revolution in 1964. That same year, it joined Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania.

## Today

Zanzibar is semi-autonomous, with its own president and government within Tanzania.
